item.title: As millions lose food aid nationwide, this SNAP office is doubling up as a food pantry
item.description: The cuts and changes to SNAP have been difficult for government workers who take pride in helping others. In San Diego, workers said they couldn't sit back while their neighbors went hungry.

item.title: Trump heads to Asia to meet with Xi and Putin amid Nvidia fallout
item.description: The trip to China marks Trump's second time this year, and comes as the president and his party faced widespread backlash from voters in the recent midterm elections.

item.title: These birds fly 17,000 miles every year. Climate change could make it harder
item.description: Migratory birds cross the entire globe, carefully timing their journeys with the seasons. In a hotter climate, that timing is increasingly out of sync.

item.title: NPR's Student Podcast Challenge is back for 2027
item.description: The annual audio competition for grades four through 12 returns in January. Now in its ninth year, the contest has involved more than 90,000 students around the country.

item.title: Why sleep matters when it comes to weight gain and loss
item.description: Sleep can have a powerful impact on weight. Research shows it can affect appetite. There is also a two-way relationship between sleep quality and diet.

item.title: Far from home. Voyager 1 is now farther than anything man has sent into space
item.description: NASA's Voyager 1, which is the furthest man-made object from Earth, is set to reach a new milestone this week. On Wednesday, the probe will be roughly 16 billion miles from Earth.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Who makes Sydney Sweeney's American Eagle jeans — and under what conditions?
item.description: Sydney Sweeney has great jeans, American Eagle Outfitters tells us. But who made them? And what are working conditions like in the garment factories of Pakistan and Bangladesh?

item.title: New Orleans port sues owners of tanker involved in Mississippi crash
item.description: Officials are seeking at least $1 million in damages from the owners of the tanker that hit a cruise ship last week. The incident was dubbed "the miracle on the Mississippi" after no one was killed.
